title: A first collaboration conversation with STXBP1 Foundation

sentences.text: At The Baker-Gordon Syndrome Foundation, we support families affected by SYT1-related disorders (Baker-Gordon syndrome), while your foundation supports STXBP1 families.
SYT1 and STXBP1 both help nerve cells release chemical messages by joining tiny storage sacs to the cell membrane.
This shared biology offers a reason to explore collaboration—not proof that the same study design will fit both communities.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Our community has a natural history study at the University of Missouri, a foundation registry, and a Cambridge/Melbourne research collaboration.
Citizen Health, RARE-X and the ENDD Center provide existing STXBP1-linked resources whose suitability we could explore together.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether these resources accept SYT1-related disorders.

Their atlas comparisons flag focal-spike EEG patterns, unusual eyebrow location and 21 other SYT1 features as unrecorded there; please check whether these occur in STXBP1, including athetoid cerebral palsy.
Please review differences flagged only on the STXBP1 side: loss of protein function, unstable or misfolded proteins, and two further unspecified mechanisms.
Several proposed protein effects remain contested, so shared biology should not imply identical effects for every genetic change.
Could Ege Kavalali review the plan, with confirmation of his SYT1 and VAMP2 work alongside his documented SNAP25 work?
Before proceeding, please also check trial enrollment and access to SYT1 animal or cell models.
Send one inquiry to STXBP1 Foundation asking whether STARR (STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready) could include SYT1-related disorders, requesting an initial eligibility assessment rather than a commitment.
Is any interventional trial enrolling people with SYT1-related disorders?
Is there a documented, accessible SYT1 animal or cell model in the atlas?
Which individual variants increase activity, impair the protein's chemical work, or cause loss of function?
Dear STXBP1 Foundation team,
Could we explore whether STARR could include SYT1 families?
Our communities share biology involved in nerve-cell messaging.
We would welcome an initial eligibility assessment this month.
Thank you for considering this small first step together.
[Your name], on behalf of The Baker-Gordon Syndrome Foundation
